data.exact_reserve_text: For the purposes of preparing these Financial Statements, the Managing Agent has adopted its external actuarial consultants' best estimate outcome. In respect of business earned at 31 December 2017, the gross and net reserves, excluding claims handling costs and run-off provision, as at 31 December 2017 total GBP 172.9 million and GBP 125.3 million respectively. During the year there was net claims development improvement of GBP 14.7 million on the 2013 and prior years, GBP 1.9 million on the 2014 year, GBP 2.7 million on the 2015 year and an improvement of GBP 0.5 million on the 2016 year of account.
data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding fell modestly in the year (opening gross reserves GBP 231.843m) with a prior-year gross release of GBP 9.29m. The release was driven by favourable claims experience identified in a comprehensive review of case reserves, notably a reduction in primary professional indemnity exposures partially offset by increases in excess layers. Reserving methodology and case reserve recalibration (including incorporation of independent actuary advice and internal case reserve changes) and the treatment of large loss loadings materially influenced the movements. Material uncertainty remains due to complex, long-running litigation on many claims.
raw_causal_phrases: The movement is largely caused by the significant decrease in the ultimate claims position of GBP 16,233k gross and GBP 14,257k net as a consequence of favourable experience over the year.

During the period, a comprehensive review of all outstanding case reserves was conducted by the Claims team to determine the expected probability and severity of a large claim emerging on a case by case basis.
This analysis revealed particular classes of business and years of account where the reserves were overly cautious or required strengthening.

The reduction in ultimate gross claims of GBP 16,233k was driven by a GBP 22,900k reduction to the primary professional indemnity account which was historically the Syndicate's largest portfolio. This was partially offset by a GBP 10,704k increase in the excess layers following the claims review.

Due to the high degree of uncertainty over the outcome of many claims due to their relative stage of development, many of which involve complex litigation over a long period, there remains significant variability in the possible outcomes.

In addition, the incorporation of the reserves advised by the independent claims consultants in 2015 and the internal case reserve increases in 2016 led to some distortion in the development patterns resulting in further variability in the range of possible future outcomes.

During the year there was net claims development improvement of GBP 14.7 million on the 2013 and prior years, GBP 1.9 million on the 2014 year, GBP 2.7 million on the 2015 year and an improvement of GBP 0.5 million on the 2016 year of account.
data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (Claims outstanding, liabilities) 2016 comparative column. Prior year development (gross) taken from Technical Provisions reconciliation row 'Changes for prior years' (Gross = (9,290)k). The report also quotes net prior-year improvements in narrative (net GBP 14.7m on 2013 & prior etc.); where narrative provided net figures these are noted in raw text but the prior_year_development_gbp_m uses the gross movement from the technical provisions table. Mapping of 'primary professional indemnity' to 'Professional Lines' and 'excess layers' to 'Reinsurance - Casualty' is an interpretative mapping and carries moderate uncertainty.
